summary: Mr. Arking discusses the history and customs surrounding the practice of staying up to study Torah on the first night of Shabuot. He details the order of study known as Tikkun Leil Shabuot, including the Tenach passages and the Idra Rabba, while noting variations in practice regarding how long to stay awake and whether to include Mishna.
questions: What is the origin of the custom to stay up on the night of Shabuot?
What is included in the Tikkun Leil Shabuot?
Should Mishna be studied on the night of Shabuot?
Is it better to stay up all night or sleep to ensure concentration for prayer?
What is the custom regarding the Idra Rabba?
